subject: Cognitive Science
title: Moral Foundations Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Moral Foundations Theory.

hook.text: Liberals stress fairness. Conservatives add loyalty and authority. Same moral sense, different weights.

buildup.text: Jonathan Haidt proposed six innate moral foundations that develop differently across cultures.

discovery.text: The six: care/harm, fairness/cheating, loyalty/betrayal, authority/subversion, sanctity, liberty.

twist.text: Haidt argues moral reasoning is usually post-hoc. We feel an intuition first, then justify it.

climax.text: Political disagreements are often foundation clashes, not logic failures. Different values, not errors.

punchline.text: Morality has many roots, not just one.

quiz.question: What does Haidt say about moral reasoning?
